does: Cooks meat or poultry slowly over low heat in a shallow earthenware dish under a tall cone lid, on a bed of sliced onion, fat and spices, with only a little water. The steam rises into the cone, cools and runs back down, so the food stews in its own juices and the sauce stays short and strong.

intro.what: A cone-lidded earthenware tagine cooks gently with restrained added water.
intro.why: The lid returns condensed steam to the dish. Keeping that cycle intact develops a concentrated sauce without treating the pot as a deep stew.

how: Spread sliced onion over the base of the dish with the fat and the spices, and pour in a little water, only enough to wet the base.
Lay the meat on top and season it. Do not brown it first.
Put on the lid and set the dish over the lowest heat, with a diffuser under it if the flame is fierce. Leave it alone and lift the lid as seldom as you can.
When the meat is tender, spread over it whatever finishes the dish, such as dried fruit, olives or vegetables, and cover again.
Cook on until the sauce has shrunk to a rich coat and the fat shines on top.

cues.text: Only a few small bubbles stir at the edge of the sauce, and a little steam rises from the top of the cone.
The meat gives way to the side of a spoon without a pull.
The scent of the spices turns round and warm, with no sharp note of scorching.

mistakes.mistake: Setting the dish on a fierce heat, which scorches the base and can crack the clay.
mistakes.fix: Start on the lowest heat, use a diffuser, and bring the heat up slowly.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring in water to cover, which makes a thin soup and washes out the taste of the spices.
mistakes.fix: Start with only a little. The lid sends the steam back down.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the lid again and again, which lets the steam escape.
mistakes.fix: Leave it covered and check only near the end.

quiz.question: What does the cone lid return to the dish?
choices: Dry oven air that browns the meat.
Oil splashed upward from the pot base.
quiz.because: Steam cools against the lid and runs back toward the food.

quiz.question: How should this tagine begin on the stove?
choices: Over fierce direct heat from the start.
With the empty clay dish heated until smoking.
Over low heat, with a diffuser if needed.
quiz.because: Gradual gentle heating protects the base and supports the restrained bubbling of this method.

quiz.question: What bubbling pattern belongs to this cooking style?
choices: Occasional small bubbles near the sauce edge.
A violent rolling boil across the dish.
Dry smoking patches around the base.
quiz.because: Quiet bubbling fits the low-heat cooking and concentrated sauce.

quiz.question: The sauce became thin after covering the food in water. What would you change next time?
choices: Add more water whenever steam reaches the lid.
Begin with less water and rely on the covered moisture cycle.
Leave the lid open throughout to release all steam.
quiz.because: The tagine returns moisture, so excessive added water dilutes the intended sauce.

comes_after.why: A tagine starts on a bed of softened onion, so a cook has to know how to soften onion in fat without colour.

variant_of.differs: Braising browns the food first and cooks it in a measured amount of liquid. A tagine skips the browning, lays the meat on a bed of onion and spices and adds only a little water, because the cone lid sends the steam back down.
